newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Cheap heating oil encouraged German buyers in June.
newsitem.headline: Cheap heating oil encouraged German buyers in June.

text.p: German heating oil consumers resumed their purchases in June after very poor spring sales and built stocks to levels slightly higher than a year ago, traders said this week.
At the end of May, private household stocks were 45-50 percent of full capacity. At the end of June they were about five percentage points higher.
This left them slightly above year-ago levels, but some four to five percentage points below the norm of the past 15 years -- 57 percent.
Traders said in June that consumers had bought as the weakness of IPE gas oil futures and a temporary dip of the dollar coincided. Trading on June 10 was particularly hectic, they said.
"Huge quantities were sold that day," said one German trader in mid-June.

In dollar terms, German inland prices have been at their a lowest levels in 18 months. In Frankfurt, for example, 100 litres of heating oil held just below $20 for almost the entire month. Last year and the year before, prices were about $1 higher.
In mark terms, the picture has been different. At around DM34 for 100 litres, prices were almost 10 percent higher than a year ago and 20 percent more than in June 1995.
However, this was well below the highs seen from October to February. In Frankfurt, prices were almost consistently above DM38 per 100 litres and surpassed DM43 at times in this period.
The growth of demand has been short-lived. This month, traders say demand has tailed off as the dollar has risen, notably since last Friday.
On Tuesday, the dollar passed DM1.80, its highest since August 1991.
While dollar quotations for Frankfurt have continued to hold below $20 per 100 litres, the price in marks has edged towards DM35.
Wholesalers and consumers, say traders, seem to be hoping and waiting for a dollar correction.
"Yes, June was good, but demand has really fallen off in July," said one German trader, reflecting the views of many.
